issues.legal_issue: A partner’s interest in a partnership firm, including an interest held as karta for a Hindu undivided family, is includible in the assessee’s net wealth.
material_facts: The assessee was assessed to wealth tax as a Hindu undivided family.
The assessee’s karta was a partner in a firm on behalf of the family.
The family’s interest in the firm was included in the wealth-tax returns.
issues.conclusion: The family’s interest in the partnership firm was property and was exigible to wealth tax as part of its net wealth.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 3, 2(m), and 2(e) of the Wealth Tax Act, 1957, read together, impose tax on the net wealth of a Hindu undivided family, including its assets, and define assets to include property of every description. A partner’s interest in a firm is property. Section 4(1)(b) concerns the prescribed manner of determining the value of an individual partner’s interest; it does not create the interest itself or make that interest taxable only for an individual assessee. The judgment identifies no earlier case by name in support of this issue.

predicates.wealth_tax_assessment_challenge: The proceeding challenges the treatment of assets in a wealth-tax assessment.
predicates.assessee_is_hindu_undivided_family: The assessee whose net wealth is being assessed is a Hindu undivided family.
predicates.family_karta_holds_partnership_interest: The family’s karta holds an interest in a partnership firm on the family’s behalf.

issues.definition: When a Hindu undivided family’s wealth-tax assessment is challenged and its karta holds a partnership interest on its behalf, that interest is included in the family’s net wealth.

issues.legal_issue: A wealth-tax officer may refer business assets for valuation when the reported book values are considered substantially below market value, notwithstanding that the partner’s interest is valued by determining and allocating the firm’s net wealth.
material_facts: The assessee was assessed as a Hindu undivided family and its interest in a partnership firm was included in its wealth-tax returns.
The firm owned buildings, and the assessee used their book values in reporting the family’s interest in the firm.
The wealth-tax officer considered the buildings’ market values substantially higher than their book values and referred them to valuation officers.
The valuation officers issued notices to the partner requesting facilities to inspect the buildings and production of related records.
The assessee challenged the valuation reference and the notices.
issues.conclusion: The valuation officer reference was justified and the related inspection and document-production notices were valid.
issues.legal_principle: Rule 2 of the Wealth Tax Rules, 1957, requires the firm’s net wealth to be determined before allocating it among the partners to value a partner’s interest. Section 7(1) provides for valuation by estimated market price. Section 7(2)(a) makes valuation of a business as a whole by reference to its balance sheet an optional method; the balance sheet is to be considered but is not conclusive, and prescribed adjustments must be made. Under Rules 2A and 2B, where market value exceeds written-down or book value by more than 20 per cent, market value is used for the prescribed business valuation. Section 7(3) and section 16A permit the valuation process involving a valuation officer, and section 38A(1)(b) supported the inspection and records notices in this case. The judgment identifies no earlier case by name; it refers generally to judicial interpretation of the phrase concerning having regard to a balance sheet.

rule.if: wealth_tax_valuation_challenge and assessee_has_partnership_interest_valued_through_firm_assets and officer_considers_reported_asset_values_substantially_below_market and officer_refers_firm_assets_for_valuation and valuation_officers_request_inspection_or_records

predicates.wealth_tax_valuation_challenge: The proceeding challenges a valuation reference or related valuation steps in a wealth-tax assessment.
predicates.assessee_has_partnership_interest_valued: The assessee’s partnership interest is valued by determining the value of the firm’s assets and allocating the firm’s net wealth among its partners.
predicates.officer_considers_reported_asset_values_: The wealth-tax officer considers the asset values reported by the assessee to be substantially below their market values.
predicates.officer_refers_firm_assets_for_valuation: The wealth-tax officer refers assets of the firm for valuation by a valuation officer.
predicates.valuation_officers_request_inspection_or: The valuation officers ask a partner to facilitate inspection of the assets or to produce related records.

issues.definition: When a wealth-tax valuation challenge concerns a partnership interest valued through firm assets, the officer considers reported values substantially below market, refers the assets for valuation, and the valuation officers request inspection or records, the reference and related notices are valid.
